result:
No, not yet: keep one deployable app and turn it into a modular monolith with enforced team boundaries, and split out a micro-frontend only where a team can show that the shared release is what is slowing it down.

Micro-frontends buy you independent deploys, fault isolation and the freedom for a team to upgrade or rewrite its slice on its own schedule. In exchange, you take on runtime integration (Module Federation or similar), version skew on React and the design system, larger bundles, cross-app routing, auth and state, harder end-to-end testing, and UX drift. That overhead usually needs a dedicated platform team, which at five teams is a large fraction of your headcount.

Most of the pain at your size comes from unclear ownership, slow CI and release coupling, and a monorepo fixes those at far lower cost. The pieces are per-team packages (Nx or Turborepo), lint-enforced import boundaries, CODEOWNERS, affected-only builds and tests, route-level code splitting, and feature flags with frequent trunk releases. This also leaves you well placed to split later, because clean module boundaries are the prerequisite for micro-frontends anyway.

Split a slice out if, after that work, a team is still regularly blocked by other teams' releases, needs a materially different release cadence or compliance isolation, or the build remains too slow despite caching. In that case, extract only that one slice.
